title: Discharge Summary and Medical Record Structuring
summary: Draft discharge summaries from the inpatient file and turn past records into structured diagnoses, procedures, medicines and allergies, each linked to its source for the doctor to verify.

seo.title: AI Discharge Summary and Record Structuring | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that drafts discharge summaries from inpatient notes, drug charts and reports, and structures past records for doctors to verify and sign.

problem.intro: A discharge summary should bring together the admission diagnosis, course in hospital, procedures, key investigations, medicines on discharge and follow-up advice. In practice a resident assembles it from handwritten progress notes, OT notes, the drug chart and lab printouts, often late in the day while the patient waits to leave. Old discharge summaries and referral letters that patients bring in stay as scanned images nobody can search.

pain_points.title: Discharge delays
pain_points.detail: Summaries written at the end of a busy shift hold up discharge, bed turnover and the insurance final bill.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent content
pain_points.detail: Different doctors include different sections, and medicines on discharge sometimes differ from the final drug chart.

pain_points.title: Unsearchable history
pain_points.detail: Scanned previous records sit as images in the HIS, so allergies and prior procedures are missed or asked again.

pain_points.title: Coding backlog
pain_points.detail: Medical records teams code diagnoses and procedures from free text, which is slow and varies between coders.

solution.overview: We build a record structuring service that reads the inpatient file and incoming past records. For discharge, it assembles a draft summary in your hospital's template: diagnosis, history, course in hospital, procedures with dates, key investigation results, condition at discharge, medicines on discharge checked against the final drug chart, and follow-up advice as the team wrote it. Each sentence links to the note or report it came from. The treating doctor edits and signs, and nothing is released unsigned. For past records, it extracts diagnoses, procedures, medicines and allergies into structured fields and suggests ICD-10 codes for the medical records team to confirm.
capabilities: Reads typed and handwritten progress notes, OT notes, drug charts and investigation reports
Drafts the discharge summary in your template with a source link on every sentence
Compares medicines on discharge with the final drug chart and flags differences for the doctor
Extracts diagnoses, procedures, medicines and allergies from past discharge summaries and referral letters
Suggests ICD-10 codes for medical records coders to confirm or change
Exports structured data to your HIS, and to FHIR-based formats where ABDM integration is in place

workflow.title: Collect the inpatient file
workflow.detail: When discharge is planned, notes, OT records, the drug chart and reports are pulled from the HIS or scanned from the paper file.

workflow.title: Extract and organise
workflow.detail: Each document is classified and its clinical facts extracted with dates and source references.

workflow.title: Draft the summary
workflow.detail: A draft is assembled in the hospital template using only facts found in the record.

workflow.title: Check consistency
workflow.detail: Medicines, procedure dates and diagnoses are cross-checked across documents, and mismatches and gaps are highlighted.

workflow.title: Doctor review and sign-off
workflow.detail: The treating doctor edits the draft, resolves each flag and signs the summary in the HIS.

workflow.title: Code and store
workflow.detail: Coders confirm suggested ICD-10 codes, and the structured record is saved for future visits.

inputs: Progress notes and OT or procedure notes
Drug chart and medication administration record
Previous discharge summaries and referral letters
outputs: Draft discharge summary with source links
Structured diagnoses, procedures, medicines and allergies
Suggested ICD-10 codes for coder confirmation
Signed summary and audit trail in the HIS
human_in_the_loop: The treating doctor reviews, edits and signs every discharge summary; no draft reaches the patient, insurer or record unsigned. Medical records coders confirm every suggested code.
integrations: Hospital information system or EMR (HL7, FHIR, API or database views)
ABDM-integrated health record systems where applicable
guardrails: Drafts use only facts present in the record, with no inferred diagnoses or advice
Every sentence carries a link to its source document and page
Unsigned drafts are watermarked and cannot be printed or shared
Role-based access aligned with HIS permissions, with patient data masked in logs
Regular MRD audit of signed summaries against source records
compliance_notes: Health data handled with consent, purpose limitation and security safeguards under the DPDP Act 2023.
Designed as a documentation aid; clinical content remains the responsibility of the treating doctor.
For US deployments, built to operate under HIPAA safeguards and a business associate agreement.

pilot.scope: Discharge summaries for one department, such as general surgery or internal medicine, drafted in parallel with the current process on de-identified or consented records.
deliverables: Template and section rules agreed with the department
Working drafting pipeline on past inpatient files
Plan for HIS integration and roll-out

what_we_measure.how: Extent of changes between the draft and the signed summary, measured on every pilot case.
Clinician review of a sample of statements against their linked sources.
Flags raised compared with discrepancies found by pharmacist or doctor review.
Time from discharge order to signed summary, compared with recent cases in the same department.

faqs.q: Will the AI write clinical opinions?
faqs.a: No. It assembles facts already in the record into your template. Clinical judgement, advice and final wording belong to the treating doctor, who signs the summary.

It handles legible handwriting in progress notes and drug charts and marks anything uncertain for the doctor instead of guessing. The pilot reports accuracy separately for handwritten and typed notes.

faqs.q: Does it work with our HIS?
faqs.a: We connect through HL7, FHIR, APIs, database views or scanned exports, depending on what your HIS vendor supports. We agree the approach with your IT team early in the pilot.
Within your infrastructure or your cloud account in an India region, using models that do not retain or train on your data. Access follows your HIS roles and is fully logged.
